verdict.rationale: Stripe's Shared Payment Tokens are a scoped grant of a customer's payment method to a specific seller. The issuing agent sets usage limits for currency, maximum amount and expiration window, and can revoke the token at any time. Link CLI also gives agents one-time-use credentials, each approved by the customer, instead of the real card details. Missing for 10: merchant restriction is only implied by the token being granted to one seller rather than documented as a configurable allow-list (and Link's virtual card explicitly works anywhere); no independent hands-on corroboration; ACS is in private preview with geographic gating.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can hand my agent a scoped, limited-use payment credential — amount limits, expiry, merchant restrictions — instead of a raw card number
